clip-1.prompt: Live-action macro realism with simple growth animation, a fixed widescreen camera, and overhead illumination. One continuous 16:9 shot, composed with space above and below for the complete young seedling. A shallow transparent planting chamber holds white granular perlite, with the seed and developing roots visible against its front face. Growth is smoothly time-compressed. 0–2 s: A dry red kidney bean rests planted in the perlite, its hard red coat and pale hilum clearly visible. Moisture wets the nearby perlite; the bean absorbs water and swells, progressively loosening its coat without making it vanish. A calm adult English narrator says exactly: "A seed takes in water." 2–5 s: A radicle emerges and extends downward under gravity, then develops small lateral roots. Two fleshy cotyledons swell as the red coat progressively slips aside, leaving attached remnants. The first leaves remain enclosed initially, then begin appearing beside the cotyledons as the shoot rises. The same narrator begins the following sentence, finishing by 7 s: "Roots grow downward, and a shoot reaches up toward the light." 5–8 s: The stem becomes upright beneath the overhead illumination. The first pair of unifoliate leaves pushes upward past the cotyledons, unfolds and expands, revealing the small terminal growing tip between them. Keep the branching roots visible below. Hold briefly on this young seedling, not a mature plant. No on-screen text, labels, dates, cuts, camera movement, music, subtitles, or additional speech.

brief: Make an 8-second widescreen explainer showing a seed sprouting. Use this exact voice-over: “A seed takes in water. Roots grow downward, and a shoot reaches up toward the light.” Simple animation, no on-screen text or music.

gate.why: This is a factual explainer; the animation should accurately show seed germination and the appearance and growth direction of roots and shoots.

research.subject: One documented botanical episode: a red kidney bean developing from a dry seed into a rooted seedling, based on the University of Nebraska–Lincoln Plant & Soil Sciences eLibrary’s day-by-day photographic sequence. The source gives days after planting, not calendar dates or a confirmed filming location. Compress approximately 12 days into an 8-second, widescreen animation; do not imply real-time growth. Suggested staging: 0–2 seconds, water uptake and swelling; 2–5 seconds, root emergence and downward growth; 5–8 seconds, shoot rising toward overhead light. Exact voice-over: “A seed takes in water. Roots grow downward, and a shoot reaches up toward the light.” No on-screen text or music.

looks.thing: Dry red kidney bean seed — day 0
looks.look: The source documents a hard outer seed coat and a hilum—the scar where the seed was attached to its pod. Inside are two cotyledons described as a big white mass, with the embryo at the seed’s tip. Figures 1–5 provide visual references; no seed dimensions are stated. ([passel2.unl.edu](https://passel2.unl.edu/revision/lesson/ecfd27c27b15/66405/5))

looks.thing: Swelling seed and loosening seed coat — days 1–2
looks.look: The seed coat swells, expands and may start slipping off, but can remain attached to the cotyledons for days. Show progressive loosening rather than an instantaneous disappearance of the entire coat. ([passel2.unl.edu](https://passel2.unl.edu/revision/lesson/ecfd27c27b15/66405/6))

A main root resembling a taproot, with lateral roots growing from it. Figure 16 documents its relationship to the emerging cotyledons and first leaves. The text does not specify root color or dimensions. ([passel2.unl.edu](https://passel2.unl.edu/revision/lesson/ecfd27c27b15/66405/9))

An upright stem with the first unifoliate leaves extending upward past the cotyledons. Figures 20–22 document the arrangement. Do not depict a fully developed plant at this stage. ([passel2.unl.edu](https://passel2.unl.edu/revision/lesson/ecfd27c27b15/66405/11))

A pair of unifoliate leaves unfolding and expanding, revealing the terminal growing tip between them. Figure 25 shows the complete young plant, including roots. ([passel2.unl.edu](https://passel2.unl.edu/revision/lesson/ecfd27c27b15/66405/12))

The documented sequence uses perlite, not ordinary garden soil; Figure 1 is the appearance reference. The text says perlite supports the seed, permits aeration and makes roots easier to view. No identifiable landscape or building is documented. A soil-cutaway presentation would be an explanatory adaptation, not a literal reconstruction of this setup. ([passel2.unl.edu](https://passel2.unl.edu/revision/lesson/ecfd27c27b15/66405/5))

The RHS documents straight upward seedling growth under overhead lighting and bending toward light arriving from one side. Use overhead illumination for the simplest upward-growing composition; no particular lamp or other physical light-source prop is documented. ([rhs.org.uk](https://www.rhs.org.uk/advice/understanding-plants/how-plants-sense-the-environment))

facts.fact: The documented subject is a red kidney bean growth sequence. At day 0, dry beans were planted in perlite, chosen to support seeds while allowing aeration and easy viewing of roots. ([passel2.unl.edu](https://passel2.unl.edu/revision/lesson/ecfd27c27b15/66405/5))
facts.when: Day 0 after planting; calendar date not stated.

facts.fact: During days 1–2, the planted bean absorbs water; its seed coat swells and may begin slipping off. This directly supports the opening voice-over sentence. ([passel2.unl.edu](https://passel2.unl.edu/revision/lesson/ecfd27c27b15/66405/6))
facts.when: Days 1–2 after planting; calendar dates not stated.

facts.fact: The sequence’s growth timeline places emergence of the radicle—the embryonic root—on day 3. Its accompanying photographic page documents emergence during days 3–4. ([passel2.unl.edu](https://passel2.unl.edu/revision/lesson/ecfd27c27b15/66405/3))
facts.when: Day 3 in the timeline; days 3–4 on the photographic page; calendar dates not stated.

facts.fact: By days 5–6, lateral roots begin forming off the radicle while the cotyledons continue swelling. The first leaves are becoming more defined but remain inside the seed coat. ([passel2.unl.edu](https://passel2.unl.edu/revision/lesson/ecfd27c27b15/66405/8))
facts.when: Days 5–6 after planting; calendar dates not stated.

facts.fact: By days 7–8, the main root resembles a taproot, its lateral roots continue growing, and cotyledons and first leaves begin appearing. ([passel2.unl.edu](https://passel2.unl.edu/revision/lesson/ecfd27c27b15/66405/9))
facts.when: Days 7–8 after planting; calendar dates not stated.

facts.fact: During days 9–10, the first leaves push past the cotyledons and rapid cell expansion makes the stems appear upright. The source also records different germination rates among the nine seeds pictured, so these timings should not be presented as universal. ([passel2.unl.edu](https://passel2.unl.edu/revision/lesson/ecfd27c27b15/66405/11))
facts.when: Days 9–10 after planting; calendar dates not stated.

facts.fact: Around days 11–12, the two first unifoliate leaves unfold and expand, exposing the terminal growing tip: a clear endpoint for the animation’s transformation from seed to young seedling. ([passel2.unl.edu](https://passel2.unl.edu/revision/lesson/ecfd27c27b15/66405/12))
facts.when: Days 11–12 after planting; calendar dates not stated.

facts.fact: Downward root growth is a response to gravity, called positive geotropism. Seedling roots and shoots can orient themselves in response to gravity after germination; do not imply that roots grow downward because they are fleeing light. ([rhs.org.uk](https://www.rhs.org.uk/advice/understanding-plants/how-plants-sense-the-environment))
facts.when: During seedling development; RHS page publication date not stated.

facts.fact: Shoots respond to both gravity and light: stems grow upward against gravity, and seedlings can bend toward a light source. Overhead lighting supports the brief’s simple image of a shoot reaching upward toward light without suggesting that underground upward orientation depends on light alone. ([rhs.org.uk](https://www.rhs.org.uk/advice/understanding-plants/how-plants-sense-the-environment))
facts.when: During seedling development; RHS page publication date not stated.

story.style: Live-action macro realism with simple growth animation, a fixed widescreen camera, and overhead illumination.
story.story:
In the opening two seconds, a fixed widescreen live-action close-up shows a dry red kidney bean planted in perlite, its hard coat and hilum visible. Simple animation compresses the documented growth sequence: the bean absorbs water, swells, and its coat progressively loosens rather than disappearing. The voice-over begins: “A seed takes in water.”

From seconds two to five, the radicle emerges and extends downward in response to gravity; lateral roots begin forming as the cotyledons swell. The first leaves remain within the loosening coat before beginning to appear alongside the cotyledons. The narration continues: “Roots grow downward, and a shoot reaches up toward the light.”

In the final three seconds, the first leaves push upward past the cotyledons on an upright stem beneath overhead illumination. The two unifoliate leaves unfold and expand, revealing the terminal growing tip, with the developing root system visible below. The sequence ends on this young seedling, without on-screen text or music.
story.title: Red Kidney Bean: Seed to Seedling
